statement: Spectral scalar curvature, Urysohn width, and macroscopic dimension. Every complete connected smooth boundaryless n-manifold, n ≥ 3, satisfying $`-4\Delta+\mathrm{Scal}\ge1`$ as a quadratic-form inequality admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $`n-2`$ whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only by n in the original metric. This strengthens Gromov's width conclusion to spectral scalar curvature. Universal covers of closed positive-scalar-curvature manifolds also have continuous macroscopic dimension at most $`n-2`$ for every n ≥ 2.
